rationale: The canonical assertion reads gateway-owned host log files and drives a host-local control topology that the nonprivileged Kubernetes client pod cannot access.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness provides a canonical gateway log evidence channel and a pod-reachable control endpoint for the duplex fixture.

re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate after a dedicated OpenLDAP sidecar or Service and an external-fixture scenario mode preserve the same protocol and certificate assertions.

rationale: The scenario loads host-local generated CA and expired client fixtures and probes numeric shared TLS listeners unavailable to the Kubernetes client pod.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness mounts the same certificate generations and exposes dedicated reachable TLS and mTLS Health Services.

rationale: The independent Go processor restricts its four listeners to literal 127.0.0.1, while the Gateway runs in another Pod; the Kubernetes harness does not deploy this processor or provide its generated CA Secret and admin endpoint, which the scenario requires.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when a Kubernetes-managed external processor with reachable TLS listeners, generated CA Secret, admin endpoint, and equivalent connection/RPC counters preserves the scenario assertions.

rationale: The canonical fixture seeds activeChallenges through ordinary resource apply, but Kubernetes owns EdgionAcme status through its status subresource; the current runner cannot inject the selected and expired challenge generations that this scenario asserts.
re-evaluation_trigger: Re-evaluate when the Kubernetes harness has an isolated status-subresource seed mechanism that preserves the ownership and expiry assertions without the live ACME controller replacing the injected challenges.
